plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with slender gray-green foliage and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields, where it attracts bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking from late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean-native; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, rough-textured stem and huge flower heads made of many tiny disc florets surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, from July through September in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and the Great Plains of the United States
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is not one flower but hundreds to thousands of tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular, many-petaled flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a waxy surface that repels water and dirt.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom from June to August during the monsoon and warm summer months
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and Vietnam, and northern Australia; also cultivated in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been shown to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the flower can regulate its own temperature to about 30-35°C.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, made of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It grows in the fynbos vegetation of southern Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from roughly May to November and a peak in winter and spring
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa; also grown in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
